newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firmer, regional index up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firmer, regional index up.

text.p: Singapore shares closed slightly firmer on Wednesday but were off the day's highs with interest largely centred around foreign shares, dealers said.
Component stocks in the newly-launched Business Times Singapore Regional Index (SRI) drew alot of interest, dealers said.
"The SRI index had a good start," one dealer with a foreign broking firm said. The SRI index was up 7.73 points or 0.79 percent to 983.22 points.
The Straits Times Industrial Index closed up 10.78 points to 2,071.26 points, off an intraday high of 2,079.26 points.
The foreign shares of DBS, SIA and UOB were the top three gainers for the day. DBS foreign was up 50 cents, SIA foreign up 40 cents and UOB foreign up 30 cents.
Singapore Press foreign, Cycle & Carriage and Creative Technology headed the losers, all down 20 cents.
Dealers said the market picked up on buying of selected blue chip counters with few institutional buyers seen.
Volume was 85.63 million shares with gainers ahead of losers by 197 to 120.
